bugs.title: [OVN] packet drops when provider network MTU exceeds tenant network MTU

blockers.summary: Regression mentioned: "…two commits in one to not introduce a regression by doing them separately. There were small changes required to unit tes…" (hudson-openstack)

The fix only takes effect when the non-default `ovn.ovn_emit_need_to_frag` option is enabled, so the reported packet drops persist on default configurations and the SRU verification steps must enable the option. It also depends on OVN support for need-to-frag, and no OVN version or dependency is documented.

The stable/2024.2 and stable/2024.1 backports combine two upstream commits into one with conflict resolutions and unit-test changes, so they differ from the upstream code. The follow-up fix for the regression bug 2105383 must be packaged together with the original change in the Ubuntu SRU, otherwise the redirect-type regression is introduced.

Earlier comments described a fuller fix (network create/update hooks, router interface attach/detach handling, and a maintenance task for existing routers). The merged change only sets the option in the router-port option generation, so already-existing routers may not be updated without a maintenance run, and the upgrade behaviour is not addressed or tested.

comments.body:
There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2026-10/msg04337.html

comments.body:
Thanks,

I will sort the changelog and the rebase on unapproved out at the time of the upload (depending of the
situation of the current unapproved upload).

LGTM

I m just wondering if that necessary to split the bug into 2 commits:
 1 - coroutine cache implementation change
 2 - follow-up fixes

This allow to avoid to have 2 references to the LP bug in the change log
and have only one changelog entry. You can use thanks to attribute the work to Alex, it is not
really important any wayu because the uploader line (with the mail) is the one that matters for the upload

comments.author: whershberger
comments.body:
Yeah, you're probably right; smth like this is probably clearer:

  [ Wesley Hershberger ]
  * Avoid guest crash with 'Cannot allocate memory' when reaching the
    vm.max_map_count limit. Thanks to Alex Ramírez (LP: #2168803)
    - d/p/ubuntu/lp2168803/coroutine-cap-per-thread-local-pool-size.patch
    - d/p/ubuntu/lp2168803/coroutine-reserve-5000-mappings.patch

    - d/control{-in}: Require QEMU apparmor profile read access for
      /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count
Do you want me to rebase and squash those commits or will you take care of it when preparing the upload?

blockers.summary: The bug has no SRU template (test plan, regression potential, etc.) and no fix or merge proposal is linked, so there is nothing to verify for stable release yet.

The only known workaround is a manual `snap set` on the cinder-volume snap, and it is reverted by `sunbeam refresh`. A charm config option is needed to make the setting persistent, and the fix must carry it through to the snap.

It is unclear whether the fix belongs in the charm, the snap, or both, and whether the option should apply to other storage backends or only Infinidat. Defaults (the snap's 4K versus Cinder's 1M) and upgrade behaviour for existing deployments are not defined.
